'''George Calef''' is a Canadian [[wildlife biologist]], author and photographer,<ref name=ggs>"Gallant's collection of short stories takes fiction prize". ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', May 18, 1982.</ref> who won the [[Governor General's Award for English-language non-fiction]] at the [[1981 Governor General's Awards]] for his nature book ''Caribou and the Barren-Lands''.<ref name=ggs/><ref>{{Cite web |title=Past GGBooks winners and finalists |url=https://ggbooks.ca/past-winners-and-finalists |access-date=2026-03-25 |website=Governor General's Literary Awards |language=en}}</ref>

Born in [[Los Angeles, California]] and educated at the [[University of British Columbia]],<ref name=pipeline>"Pipeline called caribou threat". ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', March 2, 1977.</ref> Calef worked as a wildlife biology researcher in the [[Canadian Arctic]], studying [[caribou]] for the governments of Canada and the [[Northwest Territories]].<ref name=pipeline /> In 1977, he testified before the [[Mackenzie Valley Pipeline Inquiry]] on the potential impact of the pipeline development on caribou habitat.<ref name=pipeline/>

In the 1990s, he was a co-owner of Oldsquaw Lodge, a wilderness lodge off the [[Canol Road]] near the Northwest Territories-[[Yukon]] border.<ref>"Heli-hiking in the NWT wilderness". ''[[The Globe and Mail]]'', March 25, 1995.</ref>
